title: RuleNode
description: A condition. Data, not code: storable, versionable, diffable, approvable, replayable, and showable to a regulator. Evaluation is total by construction - bounded depth (32), bounded node budget (5000), no I/O, and NO REGULAR EXPRESSIONS.

op.description: Registry key selecting an operator. The remaining properties are that operator's own arguments.

term.description: A value inside a rule. Bare JSON in an argument position is treated as a literal.

path.description: Dotted path into the resolved context, e.g. 'cart.subtotal'. A missing path resolves to undefined and never throws.

x-normative: Short-circuiting is observable: 'all' and 'any' MUST NOT evaluate children after the one that decides, and the trace MUST reflect that.
Incomparable operands (a string against money) are an error, NEVER a silent false. Returning false would hide an authoring mistake until it cost money.
A calendar field the context calendar does not publish evaluates to false, not an error, so a rule written for one calendar simply never fires on another.
There is no regex operator. String matching is a non-backtracking glob with * and ?. A tenant-authored pattern evaluated on the request path is a denial-of-service vector.
